article_title: Comparative performance of large language models in answering cornea and cataract surgery questions for resident training.
citation: Kim Seonghwan, Ji Man, Kim Chung Young, Yun Young In, Lee Gahye, Yoon Chang Ho, Kim Mee Kum. (2026). Comparative performance of large language models in answering cornea and cataract surgery questions for resident training. BMC Ophthalmology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12886-026-04767-z
title: 81-question Korean ophthalmology board-style question set on corneal diseases and cataract surgery
description: A validated set of 81 multiple-choice questions on corneal diseases and cataract surgery, built on the standard format of the Korean ophthalmology board examination and categorized into "recall-type (n = 27), interpretation-type (n = 27), and problem-solving-type (n = 27)". Answers were verified against standard reference textbooks and independently reviewed by three cornea specialists; multimodal image-based questions were excluded. The questionnaire and answers are provided in Supplementary File 1.
requirements: Questions and answers independently reviewed and validated by three cornea specialists; ambiguous questions removed or revised
constraints: Multimodal questions containing images and text were excluded due to limitations in standardized evaluation and potential variability in multimodal reasoning
target_learning_goals: clinical interpretation and problem-solving in ophthalmology
examples: Used to evaluate ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, Gemini 3.0 Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 against three residents and three cornea fellows
